phoenix.subtitle: Conference City
phoenix.title: Phoenix, Arizona

intro.label: U.S. Southwest Hub
intro.desc: Located at the heart of the Southwestern U.S., Phoenix is the state capital and the political and economic center of Arizonia.

intro.label: Modern Desert Oasis
intro.desc: Set in the Valley of the Sun within the Sonoran Desert, Phoenix blends an urban landscape with surrounding mountains and desert preserves.

intro.label: Seamless International Access
intro.desc: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) provides access to the region; the Tempe conference venue is roughly a 15–25 minute drive, depending on traffic.

stats.label: Projected Phoenix Metro Personal Income Growth

items.label: Semiconductor Cluster
items.desc: TSMC has announced a $165 billion Arizona investment, with plans for six wafer fabs, two advanced-packaging facilities, and an R&D center. The project continues to attract suppliers and talent, while Intel, KoMiCo, Fujifilm, and others are expanding their regional presence.

items.label: Emerging Technologies
items.desc: Phoenix continues to focus on advanced manufacturing, emerging technology, bioscience, and renewable energy, supported by workforce development and research partnerships.

items.label: Innovation Energy
items.desc: In 2026, Phoenix hosted the inaugural Arizona Tech Week and the Forbes Under 30 Summit, showcasing the region's momentum in entrepreneurship, investment, and advanced industries.

items.label: Core Pillars
items.desc: Beyond semiconductor manufacturing, Phoenix is developing professional services, bioscience, renewable energy, tourism, and events as part of a diversified economy.

items.label: Global Connectivity
items.desc: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) launched its first nonstop service to Asia in December 2025. Nonstop flights to Taipei now improve access for business and international visitors.

items.label: Jobs & Income
items.desc: The University of Arizona's first-quarter forecast projects Phoenix metro personal income growth of 6.3% in 2026, rebounding from 2025.

categories.heading: Demographics & Lifestyle Upgrades
categories.tagline: A new benchmark for livable cities

items.label: Population Influx
items.desc: Phoenix had an estimated population of about 1.7 million as of July 2024, making it the fifth-largest U.S. city. Continued growth is driving demand for residential and commercial space.

items.label: Quality of Life
items.desc: Dining and leisure options continue to expand across Greater Phoenix; Arizona's first Din Tai Fung opened in Scottsdale in 2026.

items.label: Diverse Lifestyle Options
items.desc: From downtown to surrounding communities, Greater Phoenix offers a broad mix of housing, work, and leisure options; living costs and commute conditions vary by city and neighborhood.

phoenix.outro: Phoenix is combining industrial strength, population growth, and comprehensive amenities to demonstrate a clear growth trajectory, securing a prominent position among U.S. cities.
